Indian History Congress moves its 85th session to Puducherry, February 2027

The annual meeting of Indian historians will not take place in Bengaluru in December. It now runs from 26 to 28 February 2027 at Tagore Government Arts and Science College, and papers are due by 7 February.

Talaash Heritage desk · Published 5 November 2026

When
26 February 2027 to 28 February 2027
Where
Tagore Government Arts and Science College, Puducherry
Apply by
7 February 2027

The 85th session of the Indian History Congress will be held at Tagore Government Arts and Science College, Puducherry, from 26 to 28 February 2027. The Congress set out the new venue and dates in a Secretary's circular dated 26 September 2026. An earlier circular, dated 10 August, had named Dr Manmohan Singh Bengaluru City University and 28 to 30 December 2026.

The change follows an urgent notice dated 3 September, signed by the Congress's Secretary, Prof. Syed Ali Nadeem Rezavi. It said the Congress had withdrawn from the Bengaluru arrangement because the university would provide only the venue and would neither appoint a Local Secretary nor seek a state grant. The later circular says instead that the university declared itself unable to host at the last minute. Both accounts come from the Congress; we have not seen a response from the university.

Under the new timetable the paper portal opens on 20 December 2026 and papers must be in by midnight on 7 February 2027. A list of papers is due online by 15 February. Late papers will not be considered, and papers cannot be handed in at the venue.

Papers may be up to 3,500 words including endnotes, with a 150-word abstract, in six sections: Ancient India, Medieval India, Modern India, Countries other than India, Archaeology, and Contemporary History of India since 1947. A member may offer one paper in one section, or two papers in two different sections. The guidelines require all authors and co-authors to be paid-up members holding a Master's degree or marksheet at the time of submission.

Membership deadlines are also later than in the August circular. Life membership (Rs 15,000), which is limited to ordinary members who have renewed for 20 consecutive years, closes at midnight on 15 December 2026. Initial ordinary membership (Rs 1,000) closes on 15 January 2027, and renewal (Rs 500) and institutional membership (Rs 5,000) on 31 January 2027. Fees exclude payment gateway charges. Members who miss the renewal date can register at the venue but cannot vote in the Executive Committee election.

The Local Secretary is Dr Sandeep Kumar Dasari. Anyone who planned around the December dates, or prepared a paper to the earlier timetable, should work from the 26 September circular.
